title: Research
text: My research interests lie at the intersection of networked systems, program analysis, and software correctness. I am particularly interested in understanding the behavior of eBPF programs as they are deployed in production systems.

title: Research
text:
eBPF bytecode analysis
Network programs may be distributed as compiled eBPF objects, and the original source code may not be available to an operator. Bytecode-based analysis can help explain which packet fields, helpers, and maps a program accesses, and how it handles different packets.
My work on Yaksha-Prashna explores static analysis and diagnostics directly over eBPF bytecode.

title: Research
text:
Network function chain verification
Real deployments frequently compose multiple network functions, such as firewalls, network address translators, load balancers, and monitoring programs. A chain can exhibit incorrect behavior even when each program appears correct in isolation.
I am investigating how to reason about execution order, early termination, packet and metadata transformations, and persistent shared maps across programs.

Making network programs easier to understand and verify
I am a PhD student in the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at IIT Hyderabad. My research lies at the intersection of networked systems, program analysis, and software correctness.
I work on analyzing compiled eBPF programs without requiring source code. I am also investigating how to reason about the behavior of network functions when they are composed into a chain.
